findings.rootCause: ValueStore.literal2data encodes the language tag verbatim and findId / BatchIdStorer.findId resolve the encoding byte-exactly (short key mdb_get, or hash + bufferEquals), while getId first consults valueIDCache whose key equality is Literal.equals (language compared with equalsIgnoreCase). Warm, "abc"@EN hits the cache entry of "abc"@en; cold (after reopen / clearCaches) it misses and resolves to UNKNOWN_ID, so FILTER(?o = "abc"@EN) and the plain pattern ?s :label "abc"@EN return no rows in BOTH pipelines, and the create path hands case variants a second id when the cache is cold.
findings.change: Design Option B (as the critique recommended): the data-to-id direction of the value dictionary is keyed by a canonical encoding whose language tag is ASCII-lower-cased (ValueStore.canonicalLanguageKey, touches only the tag segment of [LITERAL_VALUE][varint dt][dir|len or 0xC0|dir+varint len][lang][label]); the id-to-data payload keeps the spelling stored first, so lang()/export round-trip unchanged. findId, findIds/BatchIdStorer (short and hash paths; hash = hash(canonical key), payload comparison payloadMatchesKey = byte-equal outside the tag, ASCII-case-insensitive inside), the create paths and deleteValueToIdMappings all use the canonical key. The policy is persisted as StoreProperties language-tag-key=canonical|byte-exact. Legacy stores (no recorded policy) are migrated on open in one LMDB write txn: every stored language literal with an upper-case tag is re-keyed (short key delete+put, hash association remove+add); if any two ids already denote the same term (the legacy cold create path produced duplicates) the store is NOT re-keyed but recorded byte-exact with a warning naming export/re-import as the remedy, instead of silently hiding the losing id's triples (critique major on 3.1.6). This resumed session found and fixed two soundness gaps in the interrupted attempt's migration: (1) it was not idempotent - if the process stopped after the re-key commit but before store.properties was saved (LmdbStore saves after the triple store opens), the re-run counted the already re-keyed entries as collisions and flipped the store to BYTE_EXACT with lower-cased short keys, making the stored spelling unresolvable; the scan now does a canonical lookup (findId(data, key, languageRange, create) overload) and skips entries already keyed to their own id; (2) it assumed CANONICAL whenever store.properties had not been loaded, so an existing value dictionary opened with fresh properties became unreachable; the policy is now derived from the data (absent policy => byte-exact until the migration scan decides; a new store's scan is trivially empty). Also fixed a test mistake in legacyStoreWithCollidingVariantsStaysByteExact (byte-exact mode is cache-dependent by definition, so the assertion clears the cache between lookups) and made the migration's info log conditional on actually re-keyed entries. No planner-side band-aid (isSafeValuesAnchorValue unchanged).
